segments.start_exact: Crossing the Thames by Chelsea Bridge, the wanderer through London finds
segments.end_exact: Such is life at the back of York Mansions—a busy, throbbing thing.
segments.summary: Scene-setting exposition describing Battersea Park Road, Constable Plimmer's peaceful beat, and life at York Mansions.
segments.reason: Introductory descriptive/expository material establishing setting and Plimmer's situation; no scene-level GACD or ERAC within a single time/place event.

segments.start_exact: The peace of afternoon had fallen upon the world one day towards the end
segments.end_exact: Constable Plimmer paced upon his way, a blue-clad volcano.
segments.summary: Plimmer talks with Ellen on her balcony; conversation drifts to the milkman Alf, whom she admires, provoking Plimmer's jealousy and abrupt departure.

gacd.goal: Plimmer wants to connect with the attractive girl
gacd.action: He converses with her from below the balcony
gacd.conflict: She praises the milkman Alf, wounding his jealousy

segments.reason: Unified time/place (balcony conversation) with a clear goal (connect), on-stage conflict (rival milkman praise), and a disastrous emotional outcome ending with his departure.

segments.start_exact: It is a terrible thing to be obsessed by a milkman.
segments.end_exact:
This crushing truth
      Edward Plimmer learned from Ellen herself.
segments.summary: Narration of Plimmer's growing obsession with the milkman Alf and the realization that Ellen is keeping company with him.
segments.reason: Summary/bridging narration of Plimmer's brooding over time; no single-scene GACD or clear ERAC deliberation with choice.

segments.start_exact: She had slipped out to mail a letter at the pillar-box on the corner, and
segments.end_exact:
but
      Constable Plimmer was out of sight.
segments.summary: At the pillar-box Plimmer teasingly grabs Ellen's letter to Alf; a quarrel erupts, she insults him, and he confesses jealousy, disarming her before leaving.

gacd.action: He snatches the letter and confronts her about Alf
gacd.conflict: She lashes out angrily and mocks his appearance

segments.reason: Single time/place encounter with goal, on-stage verbal conflict, and an emotionally charged outcome (his admission of jealousy, both left unsettled).

segments.start_exact: Peaceful Battersea began to vex Constable Plimmer.
segments.end_exact: 'Grr-rr-rr!' he growled, and kicked the side-walk.
segments.summary: Plimmer, crossed in love, chafes at peaceful Battersea and yearns for the action of his old Whitechapel days.
segments.reason: Reflective narration of restlessness and longing; emotion present but no deliberation-plus-choice and no on-stage conflict, so narrative_scene fits better than sequel.

segments.start_exact: And, even as he spoke, on the balcony of a second-floor flat there
segments.end_exact: 'Will you come along, miss?' said Constable Plimmer.
segments.summary: Summoned by the sharp-faced woman, Plimmer investigates a theft; the accused cook turns out to be Ellen, who is charged and must be taken to the station.

gacd.goal: Plimmer answers the call and must handle the theft complaint
gacd.action: He questions the household and confronts the accused
gacd.conflict: The mistress insists on charging Ellen, whom Plimmer loves, despite her plea of innocence

segments.reason: Unified place (the flat) and continuous action with strong conflict (must arrest the woman he loves) resolving in the charge being made—clear GACD disaster.

segments.start_exact: Out in the street the sun shone gaily down on peaceful Battersea.
segments.end_exact:
In one of the flats
      a woman began to sing.
segments.summary: Plimmer walks Ellen through the street; they pass Alf, who panics and cuts her dead, pretending not to know her. Plimmer stops, moved by her misery.
segments.reason: Continuous walk through the streets with the pivotal Alf-cut-dead episode; largely narrated transition with Alf's cowardice; functions as connective narrative scene despite emotional stakes.

segments.summary: Plimmer offers to let Ellen escape at cost of his career; she refuses to ruin him, they confess feeling, and she goes to the station resolved to change and reunite with him.

cohesion.time: Continuous, that afternoon on the way to the station

gacd.goal: Plimmer tries to free Ellen and win her heart
gacd.action: He urges her to flee, then confesses his love
gacd.conflict: She refuses to let him sacrifice himself and insists on going to prison; her lingering ties to Alf

segments.reason: Continuous walk-and-talk scene with clear goal (save/win her), on-stage conflict (her refusal, his career at stake), resolving in mutual affection and her hope to reunite—an interim success.
